description: Replace the combined solver’s 4.415 ms n=352 serial-column global tridiagonal reducer with a B200 cooperative multi-CTA or thread-block-cluster design, using packed lower-triangle storage or a true band bulge chase to parallelize reflector updates and fuse the final reduction into the eigensolver while retaining both size guards and selective fallback.

Packed the n=352 lower triangle and rewired the global reducer and fused backtransform to packed indexing. The extension compiled, but validation reached n=352 and raised an output-shape error because the eigenvector allocation incorrectly inherited the 2D packed reflector shape.

Stored the n=352 lower triangle and reflector columns in packed row-major form, added a packing launch, and taught the fused backtransform to read packed reflectors. All 39 tests and the full benchmark passed; n=352 improved from parent 9757.878 to 9448.355 us and aggregate measured 43270.197 us. Nsys reduced the reducer from 4.415 to 3.839 ms despite an 86 us pack launch.

Added a four-CTA hardware block-cluster reducer over packed storage, with per-matrix cluster barriers and cached global v/y workspaces. NVCC rejected assignment of dim3 to cudaLaunchAttributeValue.clusterDim under CUDA 13.3; the attribute requires explicit x/y/z fields.

Fixed CUDA cluster-dimension attribute initialization and compiled the four-CTA reducer. The official banned-construct guard stopped validation because the source explicitly assigned the launch config's default execution-queue field; no kernel executed.

Ran the packed reducer as a four-CTA SM100 hardware block cluster per n=352 matrix, distributing matvecs, rank-2 updates, and reflector stores across 1024 cluster threads with cluster-local barriers. All tests passed, but n=352 regressed from packed single-CTA 9448.355 to 14213.160 us and aggregate to 44654.435 us. Nsys measured the clustered reducer at 8.563 ms versus 3.839 ms single-CTA, quantifying synchronization and global v/y workspace overhead.

Changed clustered n=352 reduction from four 256-thread CTAs to two 512-thread CTAs, preserving 1024 aggregate threads while halving cluster barrier participants. All tests passed; n=352 improved from 14213.160 to 13658.689 us and aggregate to 44525.602 us. Nsys reducer time moved only from 8.563 to 8.304 ms, so global workspace/barrier phases rather than cluster fanout remain dominant.

Moved clustered reducer v/y/scalars from cached global tensors into rank-0 distributed shared memory, merged reflector construction with scalar reduction, folded the y correction into rank-2 updates, and reduced cluster barriers per Householder column from six to four. All tests passed; n=352 improved from 13658.689 to 13518.543 us and aggregate measured 44465.035 us, still above packed single-CTA 9448.355 us.

Used two 1024-thread CTAs only for the first 64 largest Householder columns, then let cluster rank 1 exit while rank 0 completed the shrinking tail with block-local packed reduction. All tests passed; n=352 improved to 9404.214 us from packed single-CTA 9448.355 and aggregate to 43223.279 us. Nsys measured the hybrid reducer at 3.762 ms versus 3.839 ms for packed single-CTA and 8.304 ms for full clustering.

Reduced the hybrid cooperative prefix from 64 to 32 Householder columns, keeping the two-CTA 2048-thread cluster only for the largest active triangles. All tests passed; n=352 improved from 9404.214 to 9350.742 us and aggregate from 43223.279 to 43194.560 us.

Reduced the hybrid cooperative prefix from 32 to 16 columns. All tests passed, but n=352 regressed from 9350.742 to 9454.535 us; aggregate measured 43210.531 us with unrelated n=2048 improvement. The cooperative crossover is bracketed above 16 and below 64 columns.

Tested a 40-column clustered prefix between the 32- and 64-column points. All tests passed; n=352 measured 9386.207 us and aggregate 43230.812 us, versus 9350.742/43194.560 at 32 columns. Trial-10 nsys measured the 40-column reducer at 3.704 ms, so the 35 us end-to-end difference is within the downstream solver/run variance.

Expanded the 32-column cooperative prefix from two to four 1024-thread CTAs per matrix, raising the grid from 80 to 160 blocks to cover the B200's 148 SMs as NCU suggested. All tests passed, but n=352 regressed from 9350.742 to 11898.552 us and aggregate to 44129.941 us; the larger cluster's barrier/DSM cost outweighed grid coverage.

Restored the two-CTA 32-column hybrid and fused the lower-triangle copy into its cluster prologue, removing the standalone pack launch while using both CTAs for the copy. All tests passed; n=352 improved from the prior 32-column 9350.742 to 9335.947 us and aggregate measured 43204.840 us. Nsys shows one 3.710 ms reducer including packing, versus 3.704 ms reducer plus 86.6 us pack at the nearby 40-column point.

Replaced fused pack's inverse-triangular index mapping with warp-per-row coalesced copies to remove per-element sqrtf. All tests passed, but n=352 regressed from 9335.947 to 9474.743 us and aggregate to 43317.236 us; row/warp imbalance outweighed the arithmetic reduction.

Restored linear fused packing, split packed symmetric matvecs into branch-free lower-row and upper-column passes, precomputed packed row bases, and hoisted row correction terms in both cooperative and tail rank-2 updates. All tests passed; n=352 improved from 9335.947 to 9245.326 us and aggregate reached 43191.227 us.

Narrowed optimized packed matvec groups from eight to four lanes in both cluster and tail phases. All tests passed and n=352 validation orthogonality improved from scaled 12.9 to 5.43, but n=352 regressed from 9245.326 to 9387.171 us and aggregate to 43261.253 us. Nsys measured the reducer at 3.776 ms; eight lanes remain faster.

Fused v-dot-y accumulation into the branch-free packed matvec: each CTA writes one DSM partial, rank 0 combines them, and the single-CTA tail avoids a separate y pass and barrier. Restored eight-lane groups. All tests passed; n=352 improved from 9245.326 to 9134.970 us and aggregate to 43124.800 us. Nsys records reducer 3.752 ms, fused solve/backtransform 3.513 ms, panel 1.249 ms.

After the DSM block-partial barrier, had every CTA form the two-partial correction in registers instead of publishing it through rank 0 and synchronizing again, reducing the prefix to three cluster barriers per column. All tests passed; n=352 measured 9126.925 us versus 9134.970, within run noise, and aggregate measured 43156.707 us.

Retested a 64-column cooperative prefix after reducing cluster barriers and fusing matvec/dot work. All tests passed, but n=352 regressed from 9126.925 to 9363.505 us and aggregate to 43275.552 us; the optimized crossover remains near 32 columns.

Remapped each matvec warp to four output rows by eight inner rows so upper packed accesses become contiguous four-column segments. NVCC rejected the first source because the matvec's cluster_warp/cluster_warps locals collided with the later rank-2 update locals; no kernel executed.

Remapped packed matvec warps to four output rows by eight inner rows so upper contributions load contiguous four-column segments, with interleaved warp reduction. All tests passed and n=352 orthogonality improved to scaled 3.91, but n=352 9124.774 us was neutral versus 9126.925 and aggregate 43140.334 us. Nsys reducer time regressed from 3.752 to 3.792 ms, so tiling overhead offset improved coalescing.

Restored the simpler branch-free eight-lane matvec and set the cooperative reduction prefix to zero, retaining only two-CTA fused packing before rank 1 exits. All tests passed, but n=352 regressed from the 32-column cooperative 9126.925 to 9865.409 us and aggregate to 43364.967 us. The first 32 clustered columns therefore contribute about 0.74 ms end-to-end after tail optimizations.

Measured a 24-column cooperative prefix with the final three-barrier formulation. All tests passed; n=352 was 9206.182 us versus 9126.925 at 32 columns and aggregate 43177.908 us. Together with zero and 64 endpoints, 32 columns is the measured prefix crossover.

Restored the measured-best 32-column cooperative prefix and requested SM100 load-balancing cluster scheduling instead of the observed default spread policy. All tests passed; n=352 measured 9123.138 us and aggregate 43152.802 us, neutral versus the default-policy 9126.925/43156.707 and not better than the 43124.800 aggregate run, so scheduling preference has no measurable benefit.

Returned to default cluster scheduling and cached packed lower-triangle row offsets in per-CTA shared memory, replacing repeated triangular-index arithmetic across both the two-CTA prefix and rank-0 tail. All tests passed; n=352 improved from 9126.925 to 9056.576 us, while aggregate measured 43138.345 us and remained within unrelated-shape noise.

Added restrict qualifiers to the packed reducer buffers on top of shared row-offset caching. All tests passed; n=352 measured 9046.998 us and aggregate 43009.245 us. Mandatory nsys profiling measured the reducer at 3.670 ms versus 3.752 ms before row caching, with solve/backtransform 3.510 ms and panel 1.249 ms, confirming the reducer gain despite unrelated aggregate noise.

Specialized the clustered reducer at compile time for its only launch size n=352, folding packed extents, shared offsets, and loop bounds. All tests passed; n=352 improved from 9046.998 to 8961.149 us and aggregate measured 43049.484 us. Nsys confirmed reducer time fell again from 3.670 to 3.589 ms while solve/backtransform remained 3.504 ms.

Specialized both guarded tridiagonal eigensolver variants for compile-time n after the reducer specialization. All tests passed, but n=352 regressed from 8961.149 to 9380.331 us and aggregate to 43223.280 us. Nsys isolated the regression to solve/backtransform, which grew from 3.504 to 3.961 ms while the reducer held at 3.590 ms; fixed-size solver code generation is counterproductive.

Removed only the harmful fixed-size eigensolver specialization while retaining the compile-time n=352 reducer. All tests passed; n=352 recovered from 9380.331 to 8928.550 us and aggregate to 43041.647 us, consistent with the pre-solver-specialization candidate and confirming runtime-size solver code generation should remain.

Replaced per-element inverse triangular indexing during fused packing with equal contiguous warp chunks: each lane performed one initial square root and incrementally crossed row boundaries while preserving coalesced packed writes. All tests passed, but n=352 measured 8966.809 us versus 8928.550 for the simpler copy and aggregate 43084.561 us; extra boundary control offset fewer square roots.

Restored simple fused packing and retained shared packed-row offsets only for repeated upper-triangle matvec accesses, using direct triangular arithmetic elsewhere. All tests passed, but n=352 measured 8972.278 us and aggregate 43096.352 us. Mandatory nsys measured reducer 3.618 ms versus 3.589 ms with the full cache, proving even one-off cached address sites are worthwhile.

Restored the selected full shared row-offset cache and simple fused pack after exhausting pack and hybrid-cache variants. All 39 tests passed; final n=352 measured 8942.034 us and aggregate 43081.363 us. Fresh nsys reproduced reducer 3.589 ms, solve/backtransform 3.508 ms, and panel 1.249 ms; the reducer is down from the parent 4.415 ms and the selected source preserves all guards/fallbacks.

Exhausted the cooperative packed-reducer brief after 31 trials. Selected commit 1a731f0c664b9dbf90295b44cebfc39c9b380849: 2x1024 SM100 cluster for the first 32 Householder columns, three cluster barriers per cooperative column, fused balanced input packing, rank-0 tail, packed lower storage/backtransform, fused matvec-dot correction, full shared packed-row offset cache, restrict buffers, and compile-time n=352 reducer specialization. All 39 tests pass; final aggregate 43081.363 us, n=352 8942.034 us. Best aggregate sample was 43009.245 on the same pre-specialization line, but only n=352 changes and the specialized final repeatedly reduced n=352 further. Final nsys: reducer 3.589 ms versus parent 4.415 ms, solver/backtransform 3.508 ms, panel 1.249 ms. Explicit load-balancing scheduling, 4-CTA/2x512 clusters, longer/shorter prefixes, row-warp and incremental packing, four-lane/tiled matvec, partial row caching, and eigensolver specialization did not help. Trial24's CSV commit field is literal HEAD due a logging typo; its actual SHA is 4b121df27.
